title: By about sixty-five million years.
description:
By about sixty-five million years. The earliest shark fossils are scales roughly 450 million years old. The first trees do not appear until around 385 million years ago. Sharks got there first.

When sharks arrived, the continents were nearly bare. Land plants only crept ashore around 420 million years ago. The first sharks swam a world of bare rock and low moss, with no forest anywhere to grow.

Sharks have survived all five mass extinctions. Including the asteroid that finished the dinosaurs. It culled the largest sharks; the smaller, deeper feeders swam on, as they had through the four before it.

Four hundred and fifty million years, and the shark still owns the ocean.

Sources:
- https://www.nhm.ac.uk/discover/shark-evolution-a-450-million-year-timeline.html - The Natural History Museum, London, read in full. Established that the earliest fossil evidence for sharks or their ancestors is scales about 450 million years old (Late Ordovician), that land plants only invaded the land around 420 million years ago, and that sharks have survived all five mass extinctions, including the End-Cretaceous asteroid that ended the non-avian dinosaurs; it also notes scientists still debate whether the 450-million-year-old scales are from true sharks.
- https://www.discoverwildlife.com/prehistoric-life/are-sharks-older-than-trees - Via search summary. Established that the first trees appeared around 385 million years ago, so sharks predate trees by roughly 65 million years, and that when the first sharks appeared land plants were still low mats no taller than a few centimetres.
